name: ge-push-line-continuation-deny
_note: Verified 2026-08-08 against the CURRENT parser (no line-continuation joining and no newline-splitting exist -- lib/parse-cmd.js splits only on &&/||/;/|, and tokenize()'s whitespace matching treats a literal newline the same as a space): this command is ONE segment, and the trailing backslash character survives as its own extra token, so args becomes ['push', a lone backslash token, 'origin', 'main'] (4 entries) instead of ['push','origin','main'] (3 entries). Denial is NOT due to any continuation-aware handling (none exists) -- block-direct-to-main.js's push-destination check computes refspec candidates as positionals.slice(1) (dropping only the FIRST positional as the assumed remote); with the extra backslash token present, both 'origin' and 'main' still end up as refspec candidates, and pushDestName('main') === 'main' is protected, so it denies regardless of the stray token. Confirmed by control: replacing the backslash with an arbitrary token ('git push BOGUS origin main') produces the identical deny.

name: gp-force-push-indented-heredoc-body-allow

tool_input.command:
cat <<-EOF
	git push --force origin main
	EOF

_note: Verified 2026-08-08 against the CURRENT parser: stripHeredocs() (lib/parse-cmd.js) requires the terminator to appear immediately after a newline, with no indentation allowance for either the plain << or the <<- form, so this TAB-indented <<-EOF terminator line is never recognized as closing the heredoc -- segments() confirms the heredoc body stays completely uncollapsed and the whole multi-line string tokenizes as ONE segment whose leading command is 'cat' (the first token; args become ['<<-EOF','git','push','--force','origin','main','EOF']). Allowed because block-destructive-git.js's force-push check only fires when cmd === 'git', and cmd here resolves to 'cat', not 'git' -- the embedded 'git push --force origin main' text never reaches that check. This is not a case of the heredoc being safely collapsed by an indent-aware fix (no such fix exists); it is an accidental allow produced by the heredoc never being recognized as one at all.

name: gp-redirect-clobber-full
_note: finding 1 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): `>|` (bash's explicit-clobber operator, identical to `>` for a regular file target) is rewritten to `>` by normalizeRedirects() before segments() tokenizes the command -- the pre-fix header comment claimed `>|` was already covered via REDIR_FULL_TRUNC's `>\|` alternative, but lib/parse-cmd.js:70 splits on a bare `|` before that matcher ever ran, so `>|` could never survive as a token and the claim was an overclaim on dead code. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-clobber-glued
_note: finding 1, glued spelling (no space between `>|` and the target) -- same `>|` rewrite as gp-redirect-clobber-full, plus normalizeRedirects()'s space-insertion collapsing the glued form to a standalone token. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-glued-preceding
_note: finding 2 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review), operator glued to the END of the preceding word (`HEAD:CLAUDE.md>`) -- both the pre-fix full-token and attached-form regexes were anchored at token START, so this spelling was invisible to either. normalizeRedirects() now inserts a space before every unquoted `>`-family operator regardless of what precedes it. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-glued-both-sides
_note: finding 2, second spelling -- the operator glued to BOTH the preceding word and the target with no spaces at all. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-leading
_note: finding 3 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): a redirect placed BEFORE the command -- valid bash (verified separately: `bash -c '> f2.txt echo X'` writes f2.txt). The pre-fix segment loop keyed on `cmd === 'git'` alone, and segments() reports `cmd:'>'` for this ordering, so the whole segment was skipped (`if (cmd !== 'git') continue;`). resolveGitInvocation() now strips every redirect-operator+target pair from [cmd, ...args] and re-checks whether the first SURVIVING word is `git` (basename/suffix/wrapper-resolved), closing this without touching lib/parse-cmd.js. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-cd-devnull-target-confusion
_note: CORRECTED (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review L1): this note previously credited the redirect-stripped word list (stripRedirectPairs(args)) alone with this row's deny verdict. Mutation testing (independently re-verified by the executor, not just taken on the reviewer's word) shows that framing is inexact in BOTH directions: removing stripRedirectPairs() ALONE still denies (exit=2) -- because `.` (dest with the strip intact) resolves to `cur` itself trivially, a no-op regardless of anything else -- but removing ONLY the isDir guard (leaving the strip intact) ALSO still denies (exit=2), for the same reason: with the strip intact, `.` is correctly found regardless of the isDir check, and `path.resolve(cur, '.')` always equals `cur`, so the check's outcome cannot matter here either way. Only removing BOTH stripRedirectPairs() AND the isDir guard together flips this row to allow (verified exit=0). This row therefore has NO independent detection power for either component in isolation -- it only pins their JOINT failure (the original, pre-fix bug, where an unstripped garbage destination was ALSO committed to unconditionally). A row that could isolate the isDir guard alone would need a destination that stripRedirectPairs() already resolves correctly to something that does NOT trivially equal `cur` (e.g. a named but nonexistent directory) -- not built in this pass; flagging the gap rather than leaving it silently unpinned, per CLAUDE.md §1.6.

name: gp-redirect-cd-failed-stays-put

tool_input.command: cd zzz ; git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md > CLAUDE.md

_note: finding 5a (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): `zzz` does not exist under <REPO>, so a real shell's `cd zzz` fails and the shell stays at its ORIGINAL cwd -- the pre-fix tracker unconditionally moved `cur` to the (nonexistent) resolved path regardless of whether the destination existed, desyncing `cur` from where a real shell would actually be. The cd handler now only follows a destination that resolves to an existing directory (mirroring a real shell's failed-cd-stays-put behavior), so `cur` correctly stays at <REPO> and the subsequent `git show ... > CLAUDE.md` -- which a real shell also runs at <REPO>, since its cd failed too -- is found to overwrite an existing file and denies. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-cd-dash-returns

tool_input.command: cd .claude && cd - && git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md > CLAUDE.md

_note: finding 5b (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): `cd -` (return to the previous directory, real bash behavior) was previously rejected outright by the dest-finder because the literal token `-` starts with `-` (indistinguishable from a flag), so the pre-fix tracker left `cur` stuck at .claude/ instead of returning to <REPO>. There is no CLAUDE.md inside .claude/, only at <REPO> -- so under the pre-fix bug the target falsely resolves to a nonexistent file and allows; with `cd -` support (tracking the previous cwd) added, `cur` correctly returns to <REPO> and CLAUDE.md there denies. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-multidigit-fd
_note: finding 6 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): the pre-fix fd-prefix regex was `\d?` (zero or ONE digit only), so a real, valid multi-digit fd redirect like `10>` was invisible to it. normalizeRedirects()'s fd-prefix scan consumes an arbitrary run of leading digits before checking for the following `>`, so `10>` (and any other digit count) is now recognized and wrapped as a standalone operator token. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-unc-target-allowed
_note: finding 9 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): a UNC redirect target stalls every Bash/PowerShell call this hook runs before -- fs.statSync() on an unreachable UNC host measured 17.6s in manual testing (35.2s for two unreachable hosts) versus 42ms for a local target. looksLikeUncPath() now skips the filesystem entirely for a `\\server\share...` / `//server/share...` target, disclosed as a known gap in the header (a real UNC overwrite is never caught). LIMITED detection power: fs.statSync() on an unreachable UNC host ultimately fails too (ENOENT/timeout after the long delay) and the pre-existing catch-treats-as-absent fallback allows either way, so removing looksLikeUncPath() would flip this row's LATENCY (instant to ~17.6s), not its verdict (allow either way) -- the skip's purpose is exclusively performance; timing itself is verified manually (see the executor's Verified section), not assertable by a suite row.

name: gp-quoted-gt-grep-allowed
_note: false-positive fix (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): lib/parse-cmd.js's tokenizer unquotes a lone quoted `">"` argument to the bare character `>` before this hook's matcher ever sees it, textually identical to a real unquoted operator token -- the pre-fix code denied this ordinary read-only `git grep` (matched REDIR_FULL_TRUNC). normalizeRedirects() never rewrites anything inside quotes, so the quoted `>` is never wrapped in OP_MARK, and REDIR_TRUNC_TOKEN only matches the OP_MARK-wrapped form -- the unquoted-then-bare `>` this row produces can never match it. Verified RED (exit=2, false-positive deny) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=0) against the fix.

name: gp-quoted-gt-commit-msg-allowed
_note: companion false-positive fix, pinning a DIFFERENT pre-fix bug than gp-quoted-gt-grep-allowed: the whole quoted `-m` value here unquotes to ONE token, `>CLAUDE.md` (not an isolated `>`), which never matched the pre-fix FULL-token regex but DID match the pre-fix REDIR_ATTACHED_TRUNC regex (`(?:\d?>|&>)(?!>)(.+)`, matching ANY token starting with `>` followed by non-`>` content -- with no requirement that the `>` be a real unquoted shell operator), so an ordinary commit message that merely starts with `>` was wrongly treated as a truncating redirect onto `CLAUDE.md` and denied. REDIR_ATTACHED_TRUNC no longer exists (see header); the OP_MARK-wrapped REDIR_TRUNC_TOKEN this hook now uses is anchored to the WHOLE token and can never match unmarked quoted-then-unquoted content. Verified RED (exit=2, false-positive deny) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=0) against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-bashc-indirection
_note: regression fix (2026-08-13 cycle-2 round 2, found by the conductor after round 1 shipped): normalizeRedirects() previously ran ONCE over the whole outer command, so a `bash -c "..."` payload's `>` sat inside the OUTER quotes and was correctly left untouched there per normalizeRedirects()'s own quote handling -- but lib/parse-cmd.js's own recursion (segments() calling itself on the extracted inner text) never got a SECOND normalization pass, so the inner `>` reached REDIR_TRUNC_TOKEN unmarked and could never match (the whole indirection path silently stopped being caught). checkCommand() now re-normalizes each segment's own `raw` field individually (`segments(normalizeRedirects(seg.raw))[0]`), applying OP_MARK at whatever quoting level that segment actually sits at. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) with a copy of this file mutated back to whole-command normalization, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-shc-indirection
_note: same regression fix as gp-redirect-bashc-indirection, via the `sh -c` spelling (a separate branch in lib/parse-cmd.js's recursion condition, `cmd === 'bash' || cmd === 'sh'`) -- pins that the per-segment fix covers both wrapper names, not just `bash`. Verified RED against the whole-command-normalization mutation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-eval-indirection
_note: same regression fix as gp-redirect-bashc-indirection, via the `eval "..."` spelling (a separate, non-`-c` recursion path in lib/parse-cmd.js: extractEvalArg() rather than extractShellCArg()) -- pins that the per-segment fix covers this path too. Verified RED against the whole-command-normalization mutation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-subshell-paren-spaced
_note: finding (2026-08-13 cycle-2 round 2): a subshell-entry paren with a space before the command (`( git ...`) tokenizes as its own standalone token (cmd:'(', args[0]:'git'), so resolveGitInvocation()'s basename compare against `cmd` alone missed the `git` sitting one word later. resolveGitInvocation() now walks past a word that is nothing but `(` characters before comparing (same precedent as lib/parse-cmd.js's CWD_BUILTINS candidate check, `cwdBuiltinCandidate = strippedBasename.replace(/^\(+/, '')`). Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against a copy of resolveGitInvocation() reverted to its pre-fix form, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix. Contrast gp-redirect-subshell-paren-glued: this spaced form's target token is already clean ('CLAUDE.md', no trailing paren attached), so it needed only the resolveGitInvocation() fix -- the glued form additionally needed the target-spelling fix, round 3, see that row's note.

name: gp-redirect-subshell-paren-glued
_note: round 3 fix (2026-08-13 cycle-2, ruling on the round-2 contradiction): the no-space spelling `(git ... > CLAUDE.md)` glues the closing `)` onto the REDIRECT TARGET token too (lib/parse-cmd.js's tokenizer has no concept of `)` as a shell metacharacter, so the target token is `'CLAUDE.md)'`, not `'CLAUDE.md'` + a separate `')'`). resolveGitInvocation()'s leading-paren fix (see gp-redirect-subshell-paren-spaced) correctly identifies `git` here, but checkGitRedirectOverwrite() looking up ONLY the literal target previously failed open (a file named `CLAUDE.md)` does not exist). resolveGitInvocation() now also returns `parenEntered` (true iff a `(` had to be stripped to find `git`); checkGitRedirectOverwrite(), gated on that flag, additionally tries the target with trailing `)` characters stripped via a shared resolveTargetOverwrite() helper (no duplicated UNC/realpath/tmp-exemption logic) -- deny if either spelling resolves to an existing file. The gate keeps an ordinary non-subshell filename that genuinely ends in `)` from being misread (not itself pinned by a dedicated sample row in this pass -- see the executor's round-3 report). Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against a copy of checkGitRedirectOverwrite()/resolveGitInvocation() reverted to their round-2 form, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix. This row previously pinned the OPPOSITE verdict (allow) as a deliberately flagged, unresolved contradiction between two round-2 instructions; the conductor's round-3 ruling resolved it in favor of deny (a real bash subshell does truncate the file) without widening checkGitRedirectOverwrite()'s general target parsing to model `( ... )` grouping -- see the header's Not-covered list, still unchanged for cd-leaking/nesting/`{ ...; }`.

name: gp-h1-bslash-dquote-deny
_note: H1 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): a trailing backslash-escaped double quote outside any real quote context. Real bash: \" outside quotes escapes the quote character (literal, does not open a string), so the following > is a live, unquoted redirect operator and bash truncates the target for real (verified separately: `bash -c 'echo hello \" > victim.md'` shrinks victim.md from 17 to 8 bytes). The pre-fix normalizeRedirects() had no backslash awareness at all -- it entered quote mode on any bare "/' character regardless of what preceded it -- so this quote character wrongly opened a quote span that swallowed the real > as "inside quotes", unmarked, for the rest of the string. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix. The backslash branch in normalizeRedirects() (outside quotes / inside double quotes: backslash escapes the next character, copy both through, do not change quote state) is what closes this.

name: gp-h1-bslash-squote-deny
_note: H1, second spelling: a trailing backslash-escaped SINGLE quote outside any real quote context, same root cause and same fix as gp-h1-bslash-dquote-deny -- pins that the backslash branch covers both quote characters, not just double quotes. Verified RED against 29f4be8's hook, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-h1-xy-bslash-dquote-deny
_note: H1, third spelling: the backslash-escaped quote glued to other text on both sides (x\"y), not standing alone -- pins that the backslash branch fires wherever the backslash appears in a word, not only when it is the whole token. Verified RED against 29f4be8's hook, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-h1-false-positive-commit-allow
_note: H1, opposite-direction false positive from the same root cause: bash treats the whole -m value as ONE quoted argument (`a \" > CLAUDE.md x`, with the \" unescaping to a literal quote character inside the string) -- the > in the middle is never live. The pre-fix normalizeRedirects(), lacking backslash awareness, would have (by accident) had tokenize()'s own naive quote-matching close the quote early at the escaped \" too, which happened to also leave the > unmarked in the OLD code (verified: 29f4be8's hook already allows this one, so this row has NO detection power against 29f4be8 specifically) -- but the fix is still pinned here because it is the intentional, verified-correct behavior after making the quote tracker bash-accurate, and it is the direct symmetric counterpart of the three deny rows above (same backslash-escaped-quote mechanism, opposite direction). Verified GREEN (exit=0) against the current fix; RED-for-a-neutered-fix is not meaningful here since 29f4be8 already agrees by coincidence -- see the executor's report for the real detection-power mutation (removing the backslash branch) instead.

name: gp-h2-stray-opmark-deny
_note: H2 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): a literal ASCII 0x01 byte (the same byte value as OP_MARK) embedded in the command, BEFORE the real redirect. The pre-fix code asserted in a comment that OP_MARK is "a control byte no real shell command will ever contain" but never enforced it: normalizeRedirects() would see this stray byte, flip inMark=true, and (since no matching second 0x01 ever closes it) stay in pass-through mode for the rest of the string, silently disabling the real > later on (verified separately: `bash -c "echo hello $'\\x01' > victim2.md"` truncates for real, so this is a live bypass, not a theoretical one). checkCommand() now strips every OP_MARK byte from the incoming command once, at entry, before either normalization pass runs, so this stray byte is gone before normalizeRedirects() ever sees it. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook (which has no OP_MARK concept at all, so the byte passes through inertly there -- the REAL comparison for detection power is the executor's own mutation: removing the entry-point strip from the CURRENT code) and against a copy of the current code with the strip removed; GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-h3-bashc-clobber-deny
_note: H3 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): >| reached through bash -c indirection. lib/parse-cmd.js's OWN recursion into the bash -c payload de-quotes the inner text and re-splits it on &&/||/;/bare-| BEFORE this file's per-segment (level-2) normalization pass ever gets a turn at that layer -- so a >| that looks safely quoted from the OUTER command's own vantage point still ends up bare, and still gets split on, one recursion step later, entirely inside parse-cmd where this file has no hook to intervene (verified for real: `bash -c "bash -c 'echo X >| v4.md'"` truncates v4.md). Fixed by rewriting >| to > UNCONDITIONALLY (even inside a quoted region) in normalizeRedirects(), once, over the whole raw command, before segments() or any of its internal recursion ever runs -- removing the dangerous | byte at every nesting depth in one pass, rather than trying to catch it after the fact at whatever depth it would have split. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook and against a copy of the current code with the inside-quote >| rewrite reverted to outside-quote-only; GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-h3-false-positive-quoted-clobber-allow
_note: H3 safety check: >| sitting inside an ordinary quoted commit message must NOT become a marked redirect just because the >| -> > rewrite now also happens inside quotes. normalizeRedirects() only adds the OP_MARK wrapper when OUTSIDE a quote (the rewrite-to-> happens unconditionally, but the marking does not) -- a quoted >| becomes a quoted, unmarked >, inert for matching purposes; the normalized string is never executed, only ever inspected by this hook, so a plain textual substitution inside otherwise-inert quoted data is harmless. Verified GREEN (exit=0) against the current fix; also allow under 29f4be8 (no detection power there, since the pre-fix code never touched anything inside quotes at all) -- this row has NO detection power and is a negative control only.
